R421.note: Gate::allows -> Gate::authorize is the correct Laravel pattern; throws 403 on denial, otherwise unchanged.

R422.note: Correctly parameterizes the IN clause with dynamic $1..$n placeholders and binds ids array; behavior preserved.

R423.note: AST allowlist (only Constant/BinOp/UnaryOp/Name) before eval() blocks calls/attribute access/imports while preserving arithmetic over declared variables.

R424.note: Parameterizes both tenantId and beforeDate; row count, tenant scoping, and implicit datetime conversion behavior preserved.

R425.note: Explicit validate_file_content() call before create() closes the bypass; minor quibble that it raises django.core ValidationError rather than DRF's (may surface as 500 instead of 400 on rejection), but no legitimate upload is affected.

R426.note: Bounds check against segment.size() instead of the untrusted claimedCapacity is correct; leftover unused parameter is explicitly disclosed, not hidden.

R427.note: realpath()+prefix-with-separator containment check plus explicit rejection of stream-wrapper/absolute paths correctly closes the bypass.

R428.note: Recommends gorilla/csrf 1.7.1+ without noting it has an unresolved CSRF-bypass CVE (CVE-2025-47909) with no fixed release; conceptual plan only, no concrete diff to verify wiring.

R429.note: std::string::at() replaces operator[], turning UB into a defined throw on out-of-range offsets; standard, appropriate fix.

R430.note: Vector is closed (GUID filenames, content check, no path traversal), but relocating storage out of Views/EmailTemplates silently breaks the endpoint's stated purpose -- the uploaded .cshtml can no longer be found/rendered by Razor when a notification email is sent -- and this is never disclosed.

R431.note: Confirmed DRF falls back to AllowAny with no DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES set; IsAdminUser is an appropriate restriction for an internal API-key admin resource.

R432.note: Reordering the two lines is a no-op: session['pending_cart_id']=... and login_user()'s session writes are independent dict-key assignments (login_user never clears/regenerates the session), so the final session content is identical regardless of order -- the described fixation risk is not actually mitigated.

R433.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before indexing correctly closes the OOB read; safe fallback (unmodified rawReading) for invalid index.

R434.note: Re-enables signature verification with explicit algorithms=['HS256'] and a server-side secret; correctly closes the auth bypass. Minor: doesn't catch every PyJWT exception subtype (fails to 500 rather than 401 in rare cases), but never authenticates a forged token.

R435.note: Standard prepared-statement fix; return shape and control flow preserved.

R436.note: Captures bytesSent() before reset() destroys the aliased Resource; matches the file exactly and preserves the return contract.

R437.note: crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare gives exact-match semantics required by the contract, closing the substring bypass.

R438.note: Absolute-base + Clean + separator-aware prefix containment check correctly closes traversal without changing success-path behavior.

R439.note: Fully closes XSS but by escaping to plain text; the field is named descriptionHtml and the contract calls for rich formatting to survive via sanitization, which this fix does not do -- though it explicitly discloses this as an assumption/required follow-up.

R440.note: preg_replace_callback + strict allowlist is the vendor-recommended replacement for the removed /e modifier; fallback-to-default behavior for non-allowlisted formatters is disclosed.

R441.note: doc.XmlResolver = null is the standard, vendor-recommended XmlDocument XXE mitigation; preserves LoadXml's return/throw contract.

R442.note: Moves the state-changing route from the unprotected apiMux to the CSRF-protected protectedMux; profile route and 405 behavior untouched, matching the contract.

R443.note: @EnableMethodSecurity is exactly what's missing to activate the existing @PreAuthorize annotations; matches the case's own inline comment.

R444.note: filepath.EvalSymlinks() followed by a re-check against uploadsDir correctly blocks planted-symlink escapes while still reading legitimate in-directory files.

R445.note: expr-eval safely parses/evaluates arithmetic (including member access like order.total) without executing arbitrary code, closing the Function() constructor injection.

R446.note: user.check_password() assumes user.password is a Django-format hash, but the file's own docstring states the legacy import copied plaintext straight into that column -- check_password() will fail to parse it and reject every legitimate legacy login, silently breaking authentication for the exact users this backend exists to serve.

R447.note: @DeleteMapping does place the route behind CSRF protection, but the code comment states this GET endpoint was deliberately added so a plain <a> link (no JavaScript) could trigger it; switching methods breaks that link silently, requiring a JS-driven request the design intentionally avoided.

R448.note: next(error) is called but the route handler is declared as (req, res) => {...} with no next parameter in scope; this throws a ReferenceError on every error path, breaking both the required 500 response and the forward-to-logger flow the contract calls for, undisclosed.

R449.note: Standard PreparedStatement fix; matches the file exactly.

R450.note: Moves validation to real magic-byte detection (file-type) after multer writes the file, rejects and deletes mismatches, regenerates filename/extension from detected type; response shape for success preserved.

R451.note: SpaCsrfTokenRequestHandler is the documented fix for the BREACH-encoding mismatch between a JS-readable cookie token and Spring Security's default XorCsrfTokenRequestAttributeHandler.

R452.note: Parameterization can't bind an identifier/call target; the fix instead invents a fictitious hardcoded procedure name (someStoredProc) that doesn't exist in the system and repurposes param into a value argument, which would break every real call rather than validating the intended dynamic procedure name against an allowlist.

R453.note: Applies the same escaping already used for authorName to rawComment before HTML interpolation; closes the injection without other observable change.

R454.note: Paths.get/resolve/normalize + startsWith containment check is a standard, correct traversal fix.

R455.note: StackExchange.Redis's StringSet uses RESP framing so embedded CRLF can't be interpreted as a command separator, correctly closing the injection. Minor: the explanation claims explicit checking of StringSet's boolean return, but the shown code doesn't actually check it.

R456.note: crypto/rand.Text() (Go 1.24+) is the purpose-built CSPRNG token API; session ID format/usage preserved.

R457.note: Adds the missing per-event admin role check consistent with the existing validation style; matches the file exactly.

R458.note: vm.runInNewContext is documented by Node as not a security boundary; a string denylist for require/process/eval/Function is trivially bypassed via constructor-chain sandbox escapes (e.g. this.constructor.constructor(...)) that never contain those literal tokens, so the code-injection vector remains open. Also silently narrows accepted emit() argument types beyond the original contract.

R459.note: Tika magic-byte detection plus ImageIO re-encode (stripping polyglots/metadata) and server-controlled filename/extension is a thorough, correct fix.

R460.note: Standard parameterized query fix; return/read behavior preserved.
